clauses.scope_note: Acceptable Use Policy, lines 47–61: prohibits using, or allowing others to use, Meta Llama 3 for the listed conduct. The rights-violation category expressly includes outputs or results of products or services using Llama Materials. The sensitive-information restriction applies only without rights and consents required by applicable laws; the professional-practice restriction applies to unauthorized or unlicensed practice.
clauses.condition_explanation: licensee_accesses_or_uses_meta_llama_3 means the licensee accesses or uses Meta Llama 3, the applicability stated at line 45. The categories in requires are alternatives. The sensitive-information category covers collecting, processing, disclosing, generating, or inferring health, demographic, or other sensitive personal or private information without legally required rights and consents. The listed professional practices include financial, legal, medical/health, and related practices. Malicious-code or impairment conduct includes creating, generating, or facilitating malicious code, malware, or computer viruses, or otherwise impairing the proper working, integrity, operation, or appearance of a website or computer system.

obligation_items.content: Do not use, or allow others to use, Meta Llama 3 for any conduct in the prohibited categories.
obligation_items.actor: Licensee and persons the licensee allows to use Meta Llama 3
obligation_items.object: Meta Llama 3 and conduct or content involving its use, including covered outputs or results
obligation_items.trigger: When the licensee accesses or uses Meta Llama 3 and the use engages in, promotes, facilitates, or otherwise involves a listed prohibited category; sensitive-information handling is covered only absent legally required rights and consents, and professional practice is covered when unauthorized or unlicensed.

clauses.scope_note: Acceptable Use Policy, lines 63–69: prohibits engaging in, promoting, inciting, facilitating, or assisting in planning or developing activities presenting a risk of death or bodily harm, including the listed examples.
clauses.condition_explanation: licensee_accesses_or_uses_meta_llama_3 means the licensee accesses or uses Meta Llama 3, as stated in the Policy applicability language at line 45. The listed categories are alternatives. The military-related category includes military, warfare, nuclear industries or applications, espionage, and materials or activities subject to ITAR maintained by the U.S. Department of State. Other examples include guns and illegal weapons, illegal drugs and regulated or controlled substances, operation of critical infrastructure, transportation technologies or heavy machinery, self-harm or harm to others, and content intended to incite or promote violence, abuse, or bodily harm.

obligation_items.content: Do not use Meta Llama 3 to engage in, promote, incite, facilitate, or assist in planning or developing a covered activity presenting a risk of death or bodily harm.
obligation_items.actor: Licensee and persons the licensee allows to use Meta Llama 3
obligation_items.object: Meta Llama 3 and the covered activities or content
obligation_items.trigger: When the licensee accesses or uses Meta Llama 3 to engage in, promote, incite, facilitate, or assist in planning or developing an activity presenting a risk of death or bodily harm, including a listed example.

clauses.scope_note: Acceptable Use Policy, lines 71–78: prohibits intentionally deceiving or misleading others, including the enumerated conduct. Line 78 is a listed example of prohibited conduct, not a separately stated affirmative disclosure obligation. Impersonation is covered when done without consent, authorization, or legal right.
clauses.condition_explanation: licensee_accesses_or_uses_meta_llama_3 means the licensee accesses or uses Meta Llama 3, as stated at line 45. The listed grounds are alternatives under the prohibition on intentionally deceiving or misleading others. The final ground is failing to appropriately disclose to end users any known dangers of the actor's AI system; the text does not specify a disclosure format or timing.

obligation_items.content: Do not intentionally deceive or mislead others by a listed means, including failing to appropriately disclose known dangers of the AI system to end users.
obligation_items.actor: Licensee and persons the licensee allows to use Meta Llama 3
obligation_items.object: Meta Llama 3 and associated uses or outputs; for the nondisclosure category, known dangers of the AI system and its end users
obligation_items.trigger: When the licensee accesses or uses Meta Llama 3 and the conduct intentionally deceives or misleads others by a listed means; the nondisclosure category applies when known dangers of the AI system are not appropriately disclosed to end users, and impersonation is covered when it lacks consent, authorization, or legal right.

coverage_notes: The supplied text says the Policy applies if a person accesses or uses Meta Llama 3 and points to a most recent copy at an external URL. The contents of any later version are not supplied and are not inferred.

Lines 80–84 request reporting specified issues through listed channels. Reporting is operative request language, but no allowed activity represents reporting; this remains unresolved rather than being mapped to an inaccurate activity.

paragraph_audit.reason: Lines 47–61 are modeled, including the enumerated prohibitions, the sensitive-information qualification, the professional-practice qualification, and the express inclusion of covered product or service outputs or results.
Lines 63–69 are modeled as prohibitions on engaging in, promoting, inciting, facilitating, or assisting in planning or developing the specified risk-of-death-or-bodily-harm activities.

Lines 71–78 are modeled as a prohibition on intentional deception or misleading, including the listed examples. Failure to appropriately disclose known dangers is treated as a prohibited example, not as a separately imposed affirmative performance duty.

Lines 80–84 request reporting policy violations, bugs, risky generated content, security concerns, and unlicensed uses through listed channels. Reporting is operative request language, but no allowed activity can faithfully represent it; the reporting action remains unmodeled.
